editorial.marketOverview: Friday's regular-session close confirms a much deeper rout than the last verified afternoon observations: AP reports Nasdaq Composite down 5.3%, S&P 500 down 3.7%, and Dow down 1.9%. Nvidia, AMD, Micron and Broadcom each declined more than 12%. Reuters separately described a Nasdaq plunge around 5%, corroborating the scale of the equity selloff. Nasdaq Composite is not interchangeable with QQQ.
editorial.whatChanged: The prior 16:22 ET manual assessment lacked official closing prints and therefore retained an unconfirmed late-session selloff. AP now reports completed Friday session results showing severe semiconductor losses and broad-market spillover. This materially strengthens Monday downside-continuation risk without changing the bearish label. Curated Open Watch is unchanged at 174 events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: A broad correction driven by outsized AI and chip losses signals significant risk reduction, but does not prove a specific catalyst caused each move. Treasury yields reportedly declined and consumer sentiment improved, yet these offsets failed to prevent Friday's stock selloff. The old 10Y 4.94% and 2Y 4.65% imply an indicative +29 bp spread; neither yield is a synchronized close. VXN, closing VIX, breadth, direct FedWatch and matched oil contracts remain unverified.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23 has elevated continuation and gap risk after a confirmed Nasdaq -5.3% close, but an abrupt oversold rebound is plausible. Tuesday November 24 should determine whether semiconductor participation and breadth validate a recovery. Wednesday November 25 brings concentrated macro-event risk and could reset rate expectations. Numeric levels cannot be justified without verified current QQQ/SOX prices and volatility.
editorial.bullCase: A credible recovery needs joint QQQ/SOX or SMH strength, improving breadth and retreating VXN/VIX through Tuesday. Softer yields and oversold conditions can help, but a single sharp bounce would not invalidate the bearish three-day baseline.
editorial.bearCase: Friday's Nasdaq -5.3% and simultaneous double-digit losses in Nvidia, AMD, Micron and Broadcom confirm extreme leadership damage. A weak Monday open, failed rebound and persistent elevated volatility would favor further downside into Tuesday, with Wednesday macro releases adding gap risk.
editorial.watchNext: Verify QQQ and SOX/SMH closing returns and primary VXN/VIX/breadth; compare Monday open and close against Friday. Refresh primary 10Y/2Y and CME FedWatch and matched Brent/WTI. Confirm earnings Monday and Tuesday and Wednesday macro schedule; recheck Open Watch curated events.
